title: The trig pillar network: how Britain was measured
excerpt: I mapped all 6,573 Ordnance Survey trig pillars and tested the rule they were built to: every station must see its neighbours. Using the surveyed station heights over a modern terrain model, 95% of neighbouring primary stations still can; random lines of the same length, 11%.
seo_description: Britain's 6,573 trig pillars mapped: how far apart, when built, what survives, and can neighbours still see each other?
header_alt: Title card on cream paper reading 'The trig pillar network' beside a map of Great Britain's primary triangulation stations joined by blue lines of sight, with a few red blocked lines in eastern England.
